title: Performance Catalog Stability Gate and Pinning Playbook
creator: Dana Liu
description:
Summary:
Establish a stability gate and operational playbook for publishing Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency / throughput / cost) into the public Performance Catalog. This ticket codifies the criteria for pinning model versions, the automated checks required before publish, and a canary/rollback flow for detected regressions.

Background:
We already run verification benchmarks for model onboarding, but there is no single source-of-truth gate that asserts a profile is stable for production pinning. As models and infra change, profiles can become stale or regress due to kernel updates, quantization differences, or input distribution drift. We need a reproducible publish path and a clear stewardship model.

Scope / Outputs:
- A Stability Gate checklist and machine-readable attestation that must be satisfied before a profile moves from draft -> verified -> pinned.
- Pinning semantics: pin-by-default policy for certain tiers, and explicit pin/unpin API for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Automated verification runner job (CI) that executes latency/throughput/cost benchmarks across representative sequence lengths and hardware targets.
- Canary publish flow: staged rollout to a small percentage of runtime traffic with live-metrics comparison and automatic rollback triggers.
- Catalog metadata additions: signed artifact hash, publish timestamp, validation run id, and TTL/freshness field.
- Documentation (Confluence playbook) and an operations runbook for SRE/Oncall.

Acceptance criteria:
- The CI job runs in < 24h and produces a machine-readable attestation JSON with required fields (latency P50/P95, throughput tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens).
- A profile cannot be marked "pinned" without a passing Stability Gate and signed attestation.
- Canary publish supports: 1% -> 10% -> 100% ramp with automatic rollback on regression thresholds (latency +10% P95, throughput -15%, or cost spike >25%).
- Console shows pin status, attestations, and last-verified timestamp.
- Automation created to re-run verification on infra changes and when drift detector signals dataset shift.

Success metrics:
- 100% of newly onboarded verified profiles follow the stability gate before being published (target Q2).
- Reduce post-publish performance incidents attributable to profile staleness by 80% in quarter after rollout.
- Time-to-publish (draft -> pinned) median <= 72h for non-blocked models.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement CI verification runner and attestation schema (ENG + Research).
2) Publish playbook and pinning semantics for internal review (PM + Legal + Security).
3) Implement console UI for attestations and pin controls (Console team).
4) Pilot with 3 models (mix of small/large; hosted + dedicated).
5) Iterate on thresholds and automation based on pilot.

Automation & Monitoring:
- Drift detection hook to enqueue re-verification (linked to Optimize alerts).
- Canary controller with metrics comparison runbook and auto-rollback.
- Dashboard for pinned profiles, last-verified, and failing attestations.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Stricter gates increase time-to-publish; balance via expedited review path for security-critical or enterprise models.
- Benchmark churn from infra/kernel updates could cause noisy failures — mitigation: allow a grace window and require 2 successive failures before unpinning automatically.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Finalize attestation schema and required fields (owner: Marco).
- Create initial CI job template and performance harness (owner: Eng runtime).
- Draft Confluence playbook and runbook (owner: Dana).
